source.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה חָֽטְא֛וּ מַשְׁקֵ֥ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֖יִם וְהָאֹפֶ֑ה לַאֲדֹנֵיהֶ֖ם לְמֶ֥לֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was after these things, sinned the cupbearer of the king of Egypt and the baker against their lord, against the king of Egypt.

en.L: And it happened after these things [that] the cupbearer of the king of Egypt and the baker offended their lord, the king of Egypt.
en.B: After this, two men in the service of the king of Egypt, his cupbearer and his baker, did wrong against their master.
en.R: After a while, two men who worked for the king of Egypt did something to offend him. One was his cupbearer, who served him his wine. The other was his baker.

decisions.choice: offended: did wrong against their master
decisions.reason: The verb (chata') is the ordinary word for sin, but between people it means to wrong or offend someone. What the two men did is not told; the point is that they fell out of the king's favor.

decisions.choice: the cupbearer and the baker: officials close to the king
decisions.reason: The cupbearer served the king his wine and was a trusted court officer (Nehemiah 1:11). The baker oversaw the king's bread. Both handled what the king ate and drank, so any suspicion against them was serious.

decisions.choice: his cupbearer, who served him his wine
decisions.reason: Readable explains the office the first time it is named, then keeps the title cupbearer.

source.text: וַיִּקְצֹ֣ף פַּרְעֹ֔ה עַ֖ל שְׁנֵ֣י סָרִיסָ֑יו עַ֚ל שַׂ֣ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֔ים וְעַ֖ל שַׂ֥ר הָאוֹפִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And was angry Pharaoh at his two officials, at the chief of the cupbearers and at the chief of the bakers.

en.L: And Pharaoh was angry with his two officials, with the chief of the cupbearers and with the chief of the bakers.
en.B: Pharaoh's anger was roused against these two officials of his, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.
en.R: Pharaoh grew angry at both of these officials of his, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.

decisions.choice: his officials ... the chief of the cupbearers: senior court officers
decisions.reason: The word for "officials" (saris) is the title used of Potiphar (39:1). Each man was head over others who did the same work.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן אֹתָ֜ם בְּמִשְׁמַ֗ר בֵּ֛ית שַׂ֥ר הַטַבָּחִ֖יםאֶל־בֵּ֣ית הַסֹּ֑הַר מְק֕וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹסֵ֖ף אָס֥וּר שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he put them in custody [in] the house of the commander of the bodyguards, into the house of the prison, the place where Joseph [was] imprisoned there.

en.L: And he put them in custody in the house of the commander of the guard, in the prison house, the place where Joseph was confined.
en.B: He placed them under guard at the house of the commander of the guard, in the very prison where Joseph was being held.
en.R: He had them locked up in the house of the commander of the guard. Joseph was a prisoner in that same place.

decisions.choice: the commander of the guard: Joseph's master
decisions.reason: The title is the one given to Potiphar (37:36; 39:1), and the prison is in his house. The narrator does not say whether he still held this office or how he now regarded Joseph.

source.text: וַ֠יִּפְקֹד שַׂ֣ר הַטַּבָּחִ֧ים אֶת־יוֹסֵ֛ף אִתָּ֖ם וַיְשָׁ֣רֶת אֹתָ֑ם וַיִּהְי֥וּ יָמִ֖ים בְּמִשְׁמָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And appointed the commander of the bodyguards Joseph with them, and he served them; and they were days in custody.

en.L: And the commander of the guard appointed Joseph [to be] with them, and he attended them; and they were [some] days in custody.
en.B: The commander of the guard assigned Joseph to them, and he waited on them. They remained in custody for some time.
en.R: The commander of the guard gave Joseph the job of serving them, and Joseph looked after them. They were locked up there for some time.

decisions.choice: appointed Joseph with them: Joseph was put in their service
decisions.reason: Joseph is assigned to attend these two high officials, as he had served his master (39:4, the same verb). It also means he is the one who sees them each morning (verse 6).

decisions.choice: days: some time
decisions.reason: "Days" without a number means an indefinite time, perhaps a long one.

source.text: וַיַּֽחַלְמוּ֩ חֲל֨וֹם שְׁנֵיהֶ֜ם אִ֤ישׁ חֲלֹמוֹ֙ בְּלַ֣יְלָה אֶחָ֔ד אִ֖ישׁ כְּפִתְר֣וֹן חֲלֹמ֑וֹ הַמַּשְׁקֶ֣ה וְהָאֹפֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲסוּרִ֖ים בְּבֵ֥ית הַסֹּֽהַר׃

records.literal_gloss: And they dreamed a dream, both of them, each his dream, in one night, each according to the interpretation of his dream, the cupbearer and the baker who [belonged] to the king of Egypt, who [were] imprisoned in the house of the prison.

en.L: And they both dreamed a dream, each his own dream, in one night, each [dream] with its own interpretation, the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt who were confined in the prison house.
en.B: Then, on the same night, both prisoners dreamed, the king of Egypt's cupbearer and his baker. Each had his own dream, and each dream called for its own interpretation.
en.R: One night the king's cupbearer and baker both had dreams in prison. Their dreams were different, and each one meant something different.

decisions.choice: each according to the interpretation of his dream: each dream fit its own meaning
decisions.reason: The phrase says that each dream carried a meaning of its own, which would come true in its own way. The two dreams look alike but end very differently.

decisions.choice: they dreamed in one night: dreams come in pairs
decisions.reason: As with Joseph's own dreams (37:5-10) and Pharaoh's (41:1-7), the dreams come as a pair. In Genesis such dreams are a way God makes known what is coming.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֧א אֲלֵיהֶ֛ם יוֹסֵ֖ף בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וַיַּ֣רְא אֹתָ֔ם וְהִנָּ֖ם זֹעֲפִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And came to them Joseph in the morning and saw them, and behold, they [were] dejected.

en.L: And Joseph came to them in the morning and saw them, and look, they [were] downcast.
en.B: Joseph came in to them the next morning and could see how troubled they looked.
en.R: Joseph came to them in the morning, and he saw that something was bothering them.

decisions.choice: downcast: troubled, out of sorts
decisions.reason: The word (zo'afim) describes a troubled or sullen look; it can also mean vexed or angry.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁאַ֞ל אֶת־סְרִיסֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אִתּ֧וֹ בְמִשְׁמַ֛ר בֵּ֥ית אֲדֹנָ֖יו לֵאמֹ֑ר מַדּ֛וּעַ פְּנֵיכֶ֥ם רָעִ֖ים הַיּֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he asked the officials of Pharaoh who [were] with him in the custody of the house of his master, saying, why [are] your faces bad today?

en.L: And he asked Pharaoh's officials who [were] with him in custody in his master's house, saying, "Why [are] your faces sad today?"
en.B: He questioned the two officials of Pharaoh who were confined with him in his master's house: "Why are your faces so gloomy today?"
en.R: These officials of Pharaoh were prisoners with Joseph in his master's house. He asked them, "Why do you both look so unhappy today?"

decisions.choice: why are your faces bad?: why do you look so unhappy?
decisions.reason: A "bad" face is a sad or troubled one (compare Nehemiah 2:2). Joseph, himself a prisoner, notices the trouble of others.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו חֲל֣וֹם חָלַ֔מְנוּ וּפֹתֵ֖ר אֵ֣ין אֹת֑וֹ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם יוֹסֵ֗ף הֲל֤וֹא לֵֽאלֹהִים֙ פִּתְרֹנִ֔ים סַפְּרוּ־נָ֖א לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said to him, a dream we have dreamed, and [one who] interprets there is not of it. And said to them Joseph, [do] not to God [belong] interpretations? Recount [it], please, to me.

en.L: And they said to him, "We have dreamed a dream, and there is no one to interpret it." And Joseph said to them, "Do not interpretations belong to God? Please tell [it] to me."
en.B: "Each of us has had a dream," they replied, "and we have no one to interpret them." Joseph said, "Is it not God who gives interpretations? Please, tell me about them."
en.R: They said, "We had dreams, and there is nobody here who knows what they mean." Joseph answered, "It is God who gives the meaning of dreams. Tell me what you dreamed."

decisions.choice: there is no one to interpret it: no expert in prison
decisions.reason: In Egypt the interpretation of dreams was a learned skill, practiced by experts with written dream books (41:8). Shut in prison, the two men had no access to them.

decisions.choice: interpretations belong to God: God gives the meaning
decisions.reason: Joseph claims no skill of his own. He will say the same to Pharaoh (41:16). The word for God here is Elohim, the general word, suited to speaking with Egyptians.

decisions.choice: It is God who gives the meaning of dreams
alternatives: Do not interpretations belong to God?
decisions.reason: Readable turns Joseph's question, which expects the answer yes, into a statement.

source.text: וַיְסַפֵּ֧ר שַֽׂר־הַמַּשְׁקִ֛ים אֶת־חֲלֹמ֖וֹ לְיוֹסֵ֑ף וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ בַּחֲלוֹמִ֕י וְהִנֵּה־גֶ֖פֶן לְפָנָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And recounted the chief of the cupbearers his dream to Joseph and said to him, in my dream, and behold, a vine [was] before me,

en.L: So the chief cupbearer told his dream to Joseph and said to him, "In my dream, look, a vine [was] before me,
en.B: So the chief cupbearer told his dream to Joseph, saying, "There I was, dreaming, and before me stood a vine,
en.R: Then the chief cupbearer told Joseph about his dream: "I was dreaming, and there was a grapevine standing before me.

source.text: וּבַגֶּ֖פֶן שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה שָׂרִיגִ֑ם וְהִ֤יא כְפֹרַ֨חַת֙ עָלְתָ֣ה נִצָּ֔הּ הִבְשִׁ֥ילוּ אַשְׁכְּלֹתֶ֖יהָ עֲנָבִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: and on the vine [were] three branches; and it, as it was budding, came up its blossom, ripened its clusters [into] grapes.

en.L: and on the vine [were] three branches. And as it budded, its blossoms came up, [and] its clusters ripened [into] grapes.
en.B: with three branches on it. No sooner had it sprouted than it was in bloom, and its clusters were soon full of ripe grapes.
en.R: There were three branches on it. It started to bud, and right away flowers opened. Then its clusters turned into ripe grapes.

decisions.choice: budding ... blossom ... ripened: all at once
decisions.reason: The vine goes from bud to ripe fruit in a moment, a picture of things happening quickly. Joseph reads the three branches as three days (verse 12).

source.text: וְכ֥וֹס פַּרְעֹ֖ה בְּיָדִ֑י וָאֶקַּ֣ח אֶת־הָֽעֲנָבִ֗ים וָֽאֶשְׂחַ֤ט אֹתָם֙ אֶל־כּ֣וֹס פַּרְעֹ֔ה וָאֶתֵּ֥ן אֶת־הַכּ֖וֹס עַל־כַּ֥ף פַּרְעֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the cup of Pharaoh [was] in my hand, and I took the grapes and squeezed them into the cup of Pharaoh, and I put the cup on the palm of Pharaoh.

en.L: And Pharaoh's cup [was] in my hand, and I took the grapes and pressed them into Pharaoh's cup, and I put the cup into Pharaoh's palm."
en.B: In my hand I had Pharaoh's cup. I gathered the grapes, pressed them out into the cup, and set it in Pharaoh's hand."
en.R: I had Pharaoh's cup with me. So I picked the grapes and pressed them so that the juice ran into the cup. Then I handed it to Pharaoh."

decisions.choice: the cupbearer at work: his dream is about his own task
decisions.reason: In the dream the cupbearer does his old work, handing the king his cup. Pharaoh is named three times, and the cupbearer is active throughout, unlike the baker in his dream (verse 17).

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ יוֹסֵ֔ף זֶ֖ה פִּתְרֹנ֑וֹ שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת֙ הַשָּׂ֣רִגִ֔ים שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים הֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him Joseph, this [is] its interpretation: the three branches, three days they [are].

en.L: And Joseph said to him, "This [is] its interpretation: the three branches are three days.
en.B: Joseph said to him, "Here is the interpretation: the three branches stand for three days.
en.R: Joseph told him, "I will explain your dream. The three branches are three days.

source.text: בְּע֣וֹד׀שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֗ים יִשָּׂ֤א פַרְעֹה֙ אֶת־רֹאשֶׁ֔ךָ וַהֲשִֽׁיבְךָ֖ עַל־כַּנֶּ֑ךָ וְנָתַתָּ֤ כוֹס־פַּרְעֹה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ כַּמִּשְׁפָּט֙ הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיִ֖יתָ מַשְׁקֵֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: In yet three days will lift Pharaoh your head and will restore you to your post, and you will put the cup of Pharaoh in his hand according to the former custom, when you were his cupbearer.

en.L: Within three more days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore you to your position, and you will put Pharaoh's cup into his hand, according to the former custom when you were his cupbearer.
en.B: Three days from now Pharaoh will lift up your head and reinstate you, and you will hand Pharaoh his cup as in the old days, when you served as his cupbearer.
en.R: Before three days are over, Pharaoh will bring you out of prison and put you back in your old job. You will hand him his cup the way you used to.

decisions.choice: lift up your head: restore you to honor
decisions.reason: To lift someone's head is to raise him from a low place, here to release him and give him back his position (compare 2 Kings 25:27). Joseph uses the same words for the baker with a terrible twist (verse 19), and the narrator uses them for both men in verse 20.

decisions.choice: your post: your place or office
decisions.reason: The word (ken) means a stand or base; here it is the position the cupbearer held.

decisions.choice: will bring you out of prison
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the idiom. Balanced keeps it, because the wordplay with verses 19 and 20 depends on it.

source.text: כִּ֧י אִם־זְכַרְתַּ֣נִי אִתְּךָ֗ כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ יִ֣יטַב לָ֔ךְ וְעָשִֽׂיתָ־נָּ֥א עִמָּדִ֖י חָ֑סֶד וְהִזְכַּרְתַּ֨נִי֙ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְהוֹצֵאתַ֖נִי מִן־הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: But if you remember me with you when it goes well for you, and you will do, please, with me loyalty, and you will mention me to Pharaoh, and you will bring me out from this house.

en.L: Only remember me with you when it goes well with you, and please show loyalty to me, and mention me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house.
en.B: And once things go well for you, keep me in mind. Please do me this kindness: speak of me to Pharaoh and have me brought out of this place.
en.R: Once you are doing well again, do not forget me. Please be good to me. Tell Pharaoh about me so that I can get out of here.

decisions.choice: only remember me: an earnest request
decisions.reason: The opening words (ki 'im) here mean "only" or "but surely": Joseph asks one thing in return for the good news.

decisions.choice: show loyalty (hesed): repay kindness with kindness
decisions.reason: Hesed is the faithful kindness that people in a relationship owe one another. Joseph has served the man and brought him good news; he asks to be remembered in return.

decisions.choice: mention me to Pharaoh: bring my case to his notice
decisions.reason: The verb means to cause to be remembered. Verse 23 uses the same root: the cupbearer did not remember.

source.text: כִּֽי־גֻנֹּ֣ב גֻּנַּ֔בְתִּי מֵאֶ֖רֶץ הָעִבְרִ֑ים וְגַם־פֹּה֙ לֹא־עָשִׂ֣יתִֽי מְא֔וּמָה כִּֽי־שָׂמ֥וּ אֹתִ֖י בַּבּֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: For indeed I was stolen from the land of the Hebrews, and also here not I have done anything that they have put me in the pit.

en.L: For I was indeed stolen from the land of the Hebrews, and here also I have done nothing that they should put me in the pit."
en.B: The truth is that I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews. And here, too, I have done nothing wrong that should have landed me in this pit."
en.R: Someone kidnapped me and brought me here from the land of the Hebrews. And here in Egypt I have done nothing wrong. I should not be in this prison."

decisions.choice: I was stolen: I was kidnapped
decisions.reason: The verb, doubled for emphasis, means stolen; to steal a person and sell him was a crime punished by death (Exodus 21:16). Joseph tells the truth without naming his brothers.

decisions.choice: the pit: the same word as the cistern
decisions.reason: Joseph calls the prison a bor, the word for the pit his brothers threw him into (37:24). For the second time he is in a pit through no fault of his own.

decisions.choice: the land of the Hebrews: Canaan as Egyptians might know it
decisions.reason: Joseph names his homeland by the name of his people, as an Egyptian would understand it.

source.text: וַיַּ֥רְא שַׂר־הָאֹפִ֖ים כִּ֣י ט֣וֹב פָּתָ֑ר וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף אַף־אֲנִי֙ בַּחֲלוֹמִ֔י וְהִנֵּ֗ה שְׁלֹשָׁ֛ה סַלֵּ֥י חֹרִ֖י עַל־רֹאשִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw the chief of the bakers that good he had interpreted, and he said to Joseph, also I [was] in my dream, and behold, three baskets of white bread [were] on my head,

en.L: And the chief baker saw that he had interpreted favorably, and he said to Joseph, "I also [had a dream]: in my dream, look, three baskets of white bread [were] on my head,
en.B: The chief baker, seeing that the interpretation was a good one, said to Joseph, "I also had a dream. I was carrying three baskets of white bread on my head.
en.R: The chief baker heard the good meaning Joseph gave. So he told Joseph, "I had a dream too. There were three baskets of bread on my head.

decisions.choice: baskets of white bread: or wicker baskets
decisions.reason: The word chori appears only here. It is usually taken to mean white bread made from fine flour; others read it as wicker or open-work baskets. Either way, the baker carries baked goods for the king.

decisions.choice: he saw that he had interpreted favorably: why the baker speaks up
decisions.reason: The baker tells his dream only after hearing good news for the other man. The narrator hints that he was hoping for the same.

source.text: וּבַסַּ֣ל הָֽעֶלְי֔וֹן מִכֹּ֛ל מַאֲכַ֥ל פַּרְעֹ֖ה מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה אֹפֶ֑ה וְהָע֗וֹף אֹכֵ֥ל אֹתָ֛ם מִן־הַסַּ֖ל מֵעַ֥ל רֹאשִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: And in the basket, the uppermost, [were] some of all food of Pharaoh, work of a baker; and the birds [were] eating them from the basket from on my head.

en.L: And in the uppermost basket [were] all kinds of food for Pharaoh, the work of a baker, and the birds were eating them out of the basket on my head."
en.B: The top basket held every sort of baked food for Pharaoh, and the birds kept pecking at it from the basket on my head."
en.R: In the basket on top I had every kind of baked food for Pharaoh. But birds kept coming and eating it from the basket on my head."

decisions.choice: the birds were eating: an ill omen
decisions.reason: Unlike the cupbearer, the baker does nothing in his dream. The king's food never reaches the king, and the birds take it, as they will take the baker's flesh (verse 19).

source.text: וַיַּ֤עַן יוֹסֵף֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר זֶ֖ה פִּתְרֹנ֑וֹ שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת֙ הַסַּלִּ֔ים שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים הֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered Joseph and said, this [is] its interpretation: the three baskets, three days they [are].

en.L: And Joseph answered and said, "This [is] its interpretation: the three baskets are three days.
en.B: Joseph replied, "Here is the interpretation: the three baskets stand for three days.
en.R: Joseph answered, "I will explain your dream. The three baskets are three days.

source.text: בְּע֣וֹד׀שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֗ים יִשָּׂ֨א פַרְעֹ֤ה אֶת־רֹֽאשְׁךָ֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יךָ וְתָלָ֥ה אוֹתְךָ֖ עַל־עֵ֑ץ וְאָכַ֥ל הָע֛וֹף אֶת־בְּשָׂרְךָ֖ מֵעָלֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: In yet three days will lift Pharaoh your head from on you and will hang you on a tree, and will eat the birds your flesh from on you.

en.L: Within three more days Pharaoh will lift up your head from you and hang you on a tree, and the birds will eat your flesh from you."
en.B: Three days from now Pharaoh will lift up your head, right off your body, and hang you on a pole, and the birds will eat the flesh from your bones."
en.R: Before three days are over, Pharaoh will take off your head and hang your body on a pole. Birds will come and eat your flesh."

decisions.choice: lift up your head from you: cut off your head
decisions.reason: Joseph begins with the same words he used for the cupbearer (verse 13), but adds "from you": the head will be lifted off. The wordplay turns good news into a sentence of death.

decisions.choice: hang you on a tree: the body put on display
decisions.reason: After execution, a body could be hung on a tree or pole for all to see, a mark of disgrace (Deuteronomy 21:22-23; Joshua 10:26). The word 'ets means a tree or a wooden pole.

decisions.choice: a pole
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "tree"; Balanced and Readable say "pole", the likely form of a gallows.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗י י֚וֹםהֻלֶּ֣דֶת אֶת־פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַיַּ֥עַשׂ מִשְׁתֶּ֖ה לְכָל־עֲבָדָ֑יו וַיִּשָּׂ֞א אֶת־רֹ֣אשׁ׀שַׂ֣ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֗ים וְאֶת־רֹ֛אשׁ שַׂ֥ר הָאֹפִ֖ים בְּת֥וֹךְ עֲבָדָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was on the day, the third, the day of the birth of Pharaoh, and he made a feast for all his servants; and he lifted the head of the chief of the cupbearers and the head of the chief of the bakers among his servants.

en.L: And it happened on the third day, Pharaoh's birthday, that he made a feast for all his officials, and he lifted up the head of the chief cupbearer and the head of the chief baker among his officials.
en.B: The third day came, and it was Pharaoh's birthday. He held a banquet for all his officials, and with them all present he lifted up the head of the chief cupbearer and the head of the chief baker.
en.R: On the third day it was Pharaoh's birthday, and he held a feast for all the men who served him. With all of them watching, he had the chief cupbearer and the chief baker brought out of prison.

decisions.choice: lifted up the head of both: called them up to judge their cases
decisions.reason: Here the phrase means that Pharaoh summoned both men and dealt with them before his court. What followed differed (verses 21-22), just as Joseph had said.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh's birthday: a day of royal favor and judgment
decisions.reason: The day of a king's birth, or of his coming to the throne, was an occasion for feasting and for decisions about prisoners.

decisions.choice: his servants: his officials
decisions.reason: The "servants" of a king are his courtiers and officers, not slaves.

decisions.choice: had ... brought out of prison
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the idiom here.

source.text: וַיָּ֛שֶׁב אֶת־שַׂ֥ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֖ים עַל־מַשְׁקֵ֑הוּ וַיִּתֵּ֥ן הַכּ֖וֹס עַל־כַּ֥ף פַּרְעֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he restored the chief of the cupbearers to his cupbearing, and he put the cup on the palm of Pharaoh.

en.L: And he restored the chief cupbearer to his office of cupbearer, and he placed the cup into Pharaoh's palm.
en.B: He reinstated the chief cupbearer in his office, and the cupbearer went back to placing the cup in Pharaoh's hand.
en.R: Pharaoh let the chief cupbearer serve as cupbearer again. The man went back to handing Pharaoh his wine.

source.text: וְאֵ֛ת שַׂ֥ר הָאֹפִ֖ים תָּלָ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּתַ֛ר לָהֶ֖ם יוֹסֵֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: And the chief of the bakers he hanged, just as had interpreted to them Joseph.

en.L: But the chief baker he hanged, just as Joseph had interpreted to them.
en.B: The chief baker, though, he hanged, exactly as Joseph had explained to them.
en.R: But on Pharaoh's orders the chief baker was put to death and his body hung on a pole. Things turned out exactly the way Joseph had explained to them.

decisions.choice: just as Joseph had interpreted: the interpretation proved true
decisions.reason: Both dreams come true exactly. The God who gives interpretations (verse 8) has spoken through Joseph.

decisions.choice: the chief baker was put to death and his body hung on a pole
decisions.reason: Readable spells out both parts of what Joseph foretold in verse 19.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־זָכַ֧ר שַֽׂר־הַמַּשְׁקִ֛ים אֶת־יוֹסֵ֖ף וַיִּשְׁכָּחֵֽהוּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And not remembered the chief of the cupbearers Joseph, and he forgot him.

en.L: Yet the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph, but forgot him.
en.B: But the chief cupbearer gave no thought to Joseph; he put him out of his mind.
en.R: But the chief cupbearer did not keep Joseph in mind. Joseph slipped from his memory.

decisions.choice: did not remember ... forgot him: said twice for emphasis
decisions.reason: The narrator says it both ways. Joseph had asked to be remembered (verse 14); he stays in prison two more full years (41:1, 9).
